mainTopic: Three courtyards in a row: why the outer courtyards stay forbidden to each other, רב אשי's defense of רב יהודה and רב ששת, and רב's view that the משנה follows רבי שמעון
overview: The משנה teaches that when two outer courtyards each make an ערוב with a middle courtyard, the middle one is permitted with each of them, but the two outer courtyards stay forbidden to each other. רב ששת explains that the outer courtyards placed their ערוב in two different houses in the middle courtyard, so they never joined each other. The גמרא asks whether this follows only בית שמאי, who reject an ערוב split into two vessels. It answers that even בית הלל agree when the ערוב is split between two separate houses. Then רב אחא בריה דרב אויא tells רב אשי that both רב יהודה's and רב ששת's explanations are difficult. רב אשי answers both. The outer courtyards showed that they did not want to join each other, and the outer residents count as residents of the middle courtyard only to make things easier, never to make them stricter. Finally, רב יהודה quotes רב: the משנה's permission to carry in both directions follows רבי שמעון, while the חכמים allow carrying only from the outer courtyards into the middle one. רב יהודה then begins to report שמואל's reaction to this teaching, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of רב ששת's explanation: the ערוב was in two houses
steps.stepSummary: This line finishes רב ששת's explanation of the משנה. The two outer courtyards put their ערוב in the middle courtyard, but in two different houses.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud opens with the last words of רב ששת's explanation of the משנה. Each outer courtyard put its ערוב in a different house of the middle courtyard, so the two outer courtyards never became joined.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת explains why the outer courtyards are forbidden to each other. Their ערוב food sits in two separate houses. Because of that, the two outer courtyards are not counted as one shared ערוב, and the next step asks whose opinion this follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Food placed in one spot that joins households so they may carry together on שבת

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that an ערוב split between two houses does not join its contributors is the center of the next two steps.

phrases.english: in two separate houses.
phrases.notes: This finishes רב ששת's explanation from earlier on the daf: the outer courtyards put their ערוב in two different houses inside the middle courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב ששת's explanation of the משנה, which started on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב ששת, the outer courtyards stay forbidden to each other because their ערוב was placed in two separate houses in the middle courtyard.

steps.title: Does רב ששת follow only בית שמאי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view רב ששת follows. It suggests בית שמאי, citing a ברייתא where they reject an ערוב split into two vessels while בית הלל accept it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does this follow? בית שמאי's. As a ברייתא teaches: five people collected their ערוב and put it in two vessels. בית שמאי say their ערוב is not valid, and בית הלל say it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב ששת. His idea that a split ערוב does not work seems to match only בית שמאי, and the הלכה normally follows בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, בית שמאי say an ערוב split into two vessels does not work, and בית הלל say it does. רב ששת says an ערוב split into two houses does not work, so he sounds like בית שמאי. That would be a problem, because we do not usually explain a משנה according to בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: In accordance with whom? (Whose opinion is this?)
As it was taught in a ברייתא
The two classic schools of תנאים

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא talks about two vessels, not two houses. The גמרא is only suggesting a comparison here. The next step will point out that this difference matters.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom? With Beit Shammai,
phrases.notes: The question is really a challenge: it seems to tie רב ששת to the view we do not follow.

phrases.english: as it was taught: five people who collected their eiruv
phrases.notes: This brings a ברייתא as the source.

phrases.english: and placed it in two utensils,
phrases.notes: The ערוב was split, even though it was within one house.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: אֵין עֵירוּבָן עֵירוּב.
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: Their eiruv is not an eiruv.
phrases.notes: A split ערוב does not join the people.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say: Their eiruv is an eiruv.
phrases.notes: Splitting the ערוב between vessels does not stop it from working.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's explanation by linking it to בית שמאי's opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's explanation that the outer courtyards are not joined because their ערוב was in two houses.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rejecting a split ערוב matches בית שמאי, while בית הלל accept a split ערוב. So רב ששת seems to explain the משנה according to a view we do not follow.

steps.title: Even בית הלל agree when the ערוב is in two houses
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת can follow בית הלל. They only accept a split ערוב when both vessels are in one house, not when the parts are in two separate houses.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say this follows בית הלל. בית הלל only said their ruling there, about two vessels in one house. But in two houses, they would not say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב ששת. It shows that his case of two houses is different from בית הלל's case of two vessels in one house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל accept a split ערוב only because both parts are still in one house. In רב ששת's case the parts are in two separate houses, and even בית הלל would say that does not join people. So רב ששת fits the accepted view after all.

keyTerms.meaning: They only said it up to here (this far and no further)

steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל accept an ערוב split into two vessels within one house. An ערוב split into two houses does not work, even according to בית הלל. This keeps רב ששת's explanation standing.

phrases.english: Even if you say Beit Hillel,
phrases.notes: The defense begins: no need to tie רב ששת to בית שמאי.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי בֵּית הִלֵּל הָתָם —
phrases.english: Beit Hillel only stated their view there
phrases.notes: This limits how far בית הלל's ruling goes.

phrases.english: regarding two utensils in one house,
phrases.notes: Both parts are in one place, so they still count as one ערוב.

phrases.english: but in two houses, no.
phrases.notes: Separate houses really split the ערוב, which is רב ששת's case.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא בֵּית הִלֵּל, עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי בֵּית הִלֵּל הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 by showing that the two cases are different.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (two vessels in one house versus two houses)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ששת seemed to follow only בית שמאי, since he rejects a split ערוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even בית הלל reject an ערוב split between two houses. רב ששת follows the accepted opinion.

steps.title: רב אחא tells רב אשי: both explanations are difficult
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב אויא opens a new attack. He tells רב אשי that both רב יהודה's and רב ששת's explanations of the משנה have problems.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, son of רב אויא, said to רב אשי: There is a difficulty for רב יהודה, and there is a difficulty for רב ששת.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רב אחא announces that he has a problem with both explanations, and the next steps will spell out each problem one at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the גמרא was defending רב ששת. Now a later אמורא challenges both main explanations at once. The details come next, starting with רב יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: רב אחא, son of רב אויא, an אמורא

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַוְיָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rav Avya, said to Rav Ashi:
phrases.notes: Introduces the speaker of the new challenge.

phrases.aramaic: לְרַב יְהוּדָה קַשְׁיָא וּלְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת קַשְׁיָא.
phrases.english: For Rav Yehuda it is difficult, and for Rav Sheshet it is difficult.
phrases.notes: A general announcement. The specific problems follow.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַב יְהוּדָה קַשְׁיָא וּלְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the defense of רב ששת, a new challenge against both explanations begins.
steps.kashyaTarget: Both explanations of the משנה, by רב יהודה and by רב ששת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only announced here. Each problem is explained in the following steps.

steps.title: The problem with רב יהודה: the middle courtyard acts for both
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה said the middle courtyard placed an ערוב in each outer courtyard. But once the middle joins the first outer courtyard, they are one unit. So when the middle then joins the second outer courtyard, it should be acting for the first one too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The problem for רב יהודה: he said the case is where the middle courtyard put one ערוב in this outer courtyard and another ערוב in that one. But once the middle courtyard made an ערוב with one outer courtyard, they became one unit. So when it went back and made an ערוב with the other outer courtyard, it was acting as an agent for the first one as well.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא explains his problem with רב יהודה. If the middle courtyard joins the outer courtyards one after another, the two outer courtyards should end up joined through it. That goes against the משנה, which says they stay forbidden to each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the middle courtyard joins one outer courtyard first, the two of them become a single unit. So when the middle courtyard later joins the second outer courtyard, it does so for the whole unit, including the first outer courtyard. Then all three courtyards should be joined, so רב יהודה's case cannot explain why the משנה keeps the outer courtyards forbidden to each other.

keyTerms.meaning: It performed its agency (it acted on behalf of the first)

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not that רב יהודה's case is impossible. It is that his case leads to the opposite result from the משנה: the outer courtyards would end up permitted to each other through the middle one.

phrases.english: For Rav Yehuda it is difficult, since he said:
for example, where the middle one put its eiruv in this one
phrases.notes: Restating רב יהודה's case: the first ערוב goes into one outer courtyard.

phrases.english: and its eiruv in that one,
phrases.notes: A second ערוב goes into the other outer courtyard.

phrases.english: but once the middle one made an eiruv with an outer one,
phrases.notes: The first joining has already happened.

phrases.english: they became one,
phrases.notes: Middle and first outer courtyard now count as one unit.

phrases.english: and when it goes back and makes an eiruv with the other,
phrases.notes: The second joining, with the other outer courtyard.

phrases.english: it performs its agency.
phrases.notes: It acts for the first outer courtyard too, so all three should be joined.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first half of the challenge announced in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's explanation that the middle courtyard placed an ערוב in each outer courtyard.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After the first ערוב, the middle and first outer courtyards are one unit. So the second ערוב is made for that whole unit, and the outer courtyards should become joined, which contradicts the משנה.

steps.title: The problem with רב ששת's explanation: it should be like five residents where one forgot
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב אויא says רב ששת's explanation also has a problem. If both outer courtyards placed their ערוב in the middle courtyard, everyone becomes residents of the middle courtyard. But they used two separate houses, so they are two groups that never joined each other. That should be like five people in one courtyard where one did not join the ערוב, and they forbid each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רב ששת there is a difficulty: it should be like five people living in one courtyard, where one of them forgot and did not join the ערוב, so that they forbid one another!
steps.whatsHappening: The second half of the attack from Step 4 now hits רב ששת. Placing the ערוב in the middle courtyard should turn the outer residents into residents of the middle courtyard, and that should cause a ban on carrying instead of permission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By putting their ערוב in the middle courtyard, the outer residents are treated as if they live there. But the two outer groups used two different houses, so they never joined each other. A courtyard where some residents did not join together is forbidden to everyone, just like the classic case of five residents where one forgot.

keyTerms.meaning: Forgot and did not join the ערוב

steps.confusionAlert: The problem here is not that the outer courtyards fail to get permission. The problem is the opposite. Treating them as residents of the middle courtyard should create a new ban that would block the middle courtyard itself.

phrases.english: And according to Rav Sheshet it is difficult:
let it be like five people who live in one courtyard,
phrases.notes: Placing the ערוב in the middle courtyard makes the outer residents count as if they live there.

phrases.english: and one of them forgot and did not join the eiruv —
phrases.notes: Here, the two outer groups used separate houses, so they never joined each other.

phrases.english: where they forbid one another!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This completes the double attack announced in Step 4. Step 5 attacked רב יהודה, and this step attacks רב ששת.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's explanation that the two outer courtyards placed their ערוב in two different houses in the middle courtyard
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Putting the ערוב in the middle courtyard makes the outer residents into middle-courtyard residents. Since the two groups are not joined with each other, they should forbid one another, like the case of five residents where one forgot.

steps.title: רב אשי defends רב יהודה: the outer courtyards showed they did not want to join each other
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says neither explanation is really a problem. For רב יהודה: the middle courtyard joined with each outer courtyard, but the two outer courtyards did not join each other. That shows each one wanted to join only the middle courtyard, so the middle courtyard does not act for one outer courtyard when it joins the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: There is no difficulty for רב יהודה and no difficulty for רב ששת. For רב יהודה it is not difficult: since the middle courtyard made a ערוב with each outer one, and the two outer ones did not make a ערוב with each other, they revealed their intent. With this one they are pleased, and with that one they are not pleased.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי announces that he can answer both attacks. He starts by defending רב יהודה against the problem raised in Step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 claimed that once the middle courtyard joins the first outer courtyard, it automatically represents that courtyard when it joins the second. רב אשי answers that the outer courtyards clearly chose not to join each other. We follow what they wanted and do not force them into one combined unit.

keyTerms.meaning: He revealed his intent (his wishes became clear)
It is pleasing or acceptable to him

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to him:
It is not difficult for Rav Yehuda
and it is not difficult for Rav Sheshet.
For Rav Yehuda it is not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּעֵירְבָה לַהּ אֶמְצָעִית בַּהֲדֵי חִיצוֹנָה,
phrases.english: since the middle courtyard made an eruv with each outer one,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁתַּיִם חִיצוֹנוֹת בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי לָא עֵירְבוּ —
phrases.english: and the two outer ones did not make an eruv with each other —
they revealed their intent
that with this one (the middle) they are pleased,
and with that one (the other outer) they are not pleased.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא לְרַב יְהוּדָה קַשְׁיָא וְלָא לְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the attack on רב יהודה from Step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Intent-based answer: the parties' clear wishes decide who joins with whom.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Joining the middle courtyard with the first outer courtyard makes them one unit, so the second joining automatically includes the first outer courtyard.
steps.terutzMaskana: The outer courtyards showed that they did not want to join each other. So each joining links only that outer courtyard with the middle one.

steps.title: רב אשי defends רב ששת: they count as residents only to make things easier
steps.stepSummary: For רב ששת: the outer residents were treated as residents of the middle courtyard only to give them permission to carry. We do not use that same idea against them to create a ban.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for רב ששת it is not difficult: if they said 'residents' to be lenient, will they say 'residents' to be strict?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי now answers the attack on רב ששת from Step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling the outer people 'residents' of the middle courtyard is a tool to permit carrying. We do not turn that tool around to make them count as residents who block carrying. So the five-residents comparison does not apply.
steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי saves both explanations of the משנה. Against רב יהודה's problem, the outer courtyards did not want to join each other. Against רב ששת's problem, being counted as 'residents' is only for leniency, never for strictness.

phrases.english: And for Rav Sheshet it is not difficult:
if they said 'residents' in order to be lenient,
will they say 'residents' in order to be strict?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This finishes רב אשי's two-part answer by resolving the attack on רב ששת from Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a principle: the 'residents' status works only in the direction of leniency.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once the outer people count as residents of the middle courtyard, they should also forbid it, like residents who did not join.
steps.terutzMaskana: Resident status was given only to permit carrying. It is never used to forbid.

steps.title: רב: the משנה follows רבי שמעון, but the חכמים permit only one direction
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: the משנה's ruling that people may carry both ways follows רבי שמעון. The חכמים say one domain can serve two domains, so the outer courtyards may carry into the middle one. But two domains cannot serve one domain, so items may not be carried from the middle courtyard out to the outer courtyards.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: This is the view of רבי שמעון. But the חכמים say: one domain may serve two domains, but two domains may not serve one domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new point. It identifies whose view the משנה follows and records a stricter opinion held by the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the חכמים, carrying from either outer courtyard into the middle one is allowed, because both joined with it. Carrying out of the middle courtyard is forbidden, because it is tied to both outer courtyards at once. Bringing its items into one outer courtyard would count as taking them away from the other.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a dispute between רבי שמעון and the חכמים about carrying in a row of courtyards. The rest of the סוגיא will likely discuss it.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
This is the statement of Rabbi Shimon.
phrases.notes: This refers to the משנה's ruling that people may carry both into and out of the middle courtyard.

phrases.english: But the Sages say:
One domain serves two domains.
phrases.notes: So the outer courtyards may carry into the middle one.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לָא שְׁתֵּי רְשׁוּיוֹת מְשַׁמְּשׁוֹת לִרְשׁוּת אַחַת.
phrases.english: But two domains do not serve one domain.
phrases.notes: So items may not be carried from the middle courtyard out to the outer ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This begins a new topic after the cycle of attacks and answers is resolved. It identifies whose view the משנה follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's two-way permission follows רבי שמעון. The חכמים allow carrying only from the outer courtyards into the middle one, not from the middle one outward.

steps.title: רב יהודה brings רב's teaching to שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says that when he repeated רב's teaching before שמואל, שמואל replied to him. This line sets up שמואל's reply, which comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I said this teaching in front of שמואל, he said to me:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רב יהודה tells us he repeated רב's teaching before שמואל, and the גמרא is getting ready to quote שמואל's reaction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching being discussed is from Step 9: רב said the משנה follows רבי שמעון, and the חכמים would not allow carrying from the middle courtyard out to the outer ones. רב יהודה learned from both רב and שמואל, so he checked this teaching with his other teacher. The words 'he said to me' tell us that שמואל's own view is about to be stated.

keyTerms.meaning: I said it / I repeated it (the teaching)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop here thinking something was decided. This line gives no ruling. It only opens the door to what שמואל says next.

phrases.english: When I said it in front of Shmuel,
phrases.notes: The speaker is רב יהודה. 'It' means רב's teaching from Step 9.

phrases.english: he said to me:
phrases.notes: Introduces שמואל's reply, which appears on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אַמְרִיתַהּ קַמֵּיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל, אֲמַר לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רב's teaching from Step 9 and brings it before a second teacher, שמואל, to introduce his reaction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no ruling yet. This is only a report that רב יהודה brought רב's teaching to שמואל. The substance of שמואל's answer follows on the next amud.
